title: Ring-presheaf sheafification commutes with localization of a site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $U$ be an object. Take rings in a universe containing the objects and morphisms of $\mathcal C$. For a presheaf of rings $P:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Ring}$, let $P|_U(V\to U)=P(V)$ with the same restriction maps, and let $(-)^\#$ denote ring-valued sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. On the localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] there is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings $e_P:(P|_U)^\#\xrightarrow{\sim}(P^\#)|_U$, natural in $P$. If $\eta_P:P\to P^\#$ is the sheafification unit, then $e_P\circ\eta_{P|_U}=(\eta_P)|_U$ as morphisms of ring presheaves on $\mathcal C/U$.

mathlib_match.how: Specializes in one line per clause: take G = Over.forget U, J = the slice topology, K = the original topology, A = RingCat. The natural isomorphism is at lines 382-386; its unit identity is at lines 391-411. Over.forget is cocontinuous and continuous by Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Over.lean:279-286, and overPullback at lines 289-291 is restriction. RingCat.hasLimitsOfSize and RingCat.hasLimits at Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Ring/Limits.lean:355-359 supply pointwise right Kan extensions on the small comma categories; the coefficient universe contains the site. RingCat sheafification follows from the concrete-category instance Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/LeftExact.lean:308-311 and RingCat.forget_preservesLimits at Ring/Limits.lean:403. Thus all inferred hypotheses of both displayed declarations hold. The remaining concrete-sheafification hypotheses at LeftExact.lean:246-255 are supplied by RingCat.Colimits.hasColimits_ringCat (Ring/Colimits.lean:287-292), RingCat.FilteredColimits.forget_preservesFilteredColimits (Ring/FilteredColimits.lean:309-310), and RingCat.forgetReflectIsos (Ring/Basic.lean:360-366). The opposite covering posets are filtered, and are small in the stated coefficient universe; all their limits and colimits can therefore be formed there.
